action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

The current board shows opponent 'x' pieces at the bottom of columns 2 and 3, with my 'o' directly above the piece in column 3. This creates an immediate danger: if I play anywhere other than column 1 or 4, 'x' can respond in column 4 to create three consecutive 'x' pieces along the bottom row (columns 2-4). This would generate an unblockable fork with winning threats in both column 1 and column 5 on their next turn.

I must therefore occupy one of the extension points now. Among the two options, column 4 is superior because:
- It directly blocks the right-side extension that would enable the fork.
- It places my new 'o' diagonally adjacent to my existing piece at row 4/column 3, building a potential diagonal line for future threats.
- Column 1 blocks the left extension but creates no such connection and leaves my pieces more isolated.

No other column prevents the fork or improves my position, and I have no immediate winning move of my own. Column 4 is therefore optimal.

action.thoughts:
The current board has only four pieces placed, all near the bottom in columns 3-5, so this is still a very open position with no immediate wins or forced blocks possible on the next turn. Player O already controls (3,4) directly above an X and has an additional O at (5,5). Player X has two adjacent pieces at (3,5) and (4,5).

The key strategic observation is that column 4 is currently open above the X at (4,5). If O does not claim it, X can immediately occupy (4,4) on the following turn. That would give X a strong L-shaped formation of three X pieces: (3,5), (4,5), and (4,4). Such a structure creates multiple follow-up threats (horizontal extension left, vertical extension upward, and diagonal options) that would be difficult to defend.

By contrast, O dropping in column 4 places an O at (4,4). This achieves three positive outcomes simultaneously:
- It preemptively denies X the strong (4,4) square.
- It connects horizontally with the existing O at (3,4), creating two adjacent O pieces on row 4.
- It sits diagonally adjacent to the O at (5,5), forming a flexible structure that can later be extended into multiple lines (horizontal on row 4 or diagonal).

Alternative moves are inferior:
- Column 3 adds a vertical O but leaves (4,4) available for X, allowing the dangerous L-shape described above.
- Column 5 adds a vertical pair in column 5 but leaves a gap at (4,4) and is less central.
- Columns 0, 1, 2, or 6 are too far from the existing pieces and do not contest the critical central squares or prevent X's follow-up.

After O plays column 4, the resulting position favors O: two O pieces sit directly above X's pair, the center is contested, and X has no immediate counter-threat. Subsequent play can focus on extending the row-4 O pair or the diagonal while responding to X's attempts to open new lines.

Final Answer: 4
